name: DIY gap bands
lead: DIY gap bands are small elastic bands that people place around teeth at home to try to close the gap between the front teeth (a diastema) without seeing a dentist. The aim is a gap-free, more even smile, a change people associate with a neater, more conventionally attractive look, achieved at very low cost.

A diastema is a space between teeth, most often the upper front teeth. Wikipedia lists causes including a prominent lip frenulum, tongue thrusting, gum disease, an extra tooth and a mismatch of jaw growth, and states that a diastema is not a pathology and any treatment is cosmetic; options include orthodontics, bonding, or veneers and crowns [2]. In professional orthodontics, forces are applied to teeth with elastics and springs through fixed appliances that a clinician adjusts [1].
No published studies of the home practice were found, so what the bands do outside clinical supervision has not been described in research.

paras: The practice involves looping a small elastic band around teeth next to a gap so the band pulls them together. It is a home adaptation of the idea behind orthodontic elastics and is usually performed without a dentist.

Diastemata are common in children and can persist into adult teeth, and they occur normally in many mammal species [2]. Causes named by Wikipedia include a lip frenulum that extends between the teeth, tongue thrusting, periodontal bone loss, an extra tooth behind the front teeth, a skeletal mismatch between the jaws and forward-angled front teeth [2]. Because causes differ, treatment in clinics targets the underlying cause and varies by patient [2].

Orthodontic references describe elastics, springs and ligatures as forces applied through fixed appliances under clinician adjustment, and note that springs can be used to close gaps [1]. Wikipedia says fixed appliances give greater mechanical control of teeth and that forces can be applied using elastic bands [1]. It also states that the effectiveness of mail-order clear aligners lacks sufficient evidence [1].

card.summary: Home elastic bands aimed at closing tooth gaps; no studies exist.

quick.overview:
People try to close gaps between teeth by placing small elastic bands around them at home.

No research on the practice was found.
quick.mechanism: The band is intended to apply inward force; in clinics, such forces are applied by supervised appliances [1].

chain: Elastic band placed around the teeth bordering the gap
Band applies inward pressure over time
Gap between front teeth narrows, giving a more even smile
angle.text: People use gap bands hoping to close a space between the front teeth cheaply at home, aiming for a more uniform smile. The same goal is pursued in clinics with braces, bonding or veneers.
